faq.q: What is the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS)?
faq.a: The LRS is an RBI framework allowing resident individuals to remit up to USD 250,000 per financial year (April-March) for various permissible current and capital account transactions, including travel, education, medical treatment, and investments.

faq.q: How does TCS on foreign travel work from April 1, 2026?
faq.a: From April 1, 2026, overseas tour packages attract a flat 2% TCS from the first rupee. For other LRS remittances (like forex card loading, direct travel expenses), there is no TCS up to ₹10 lakh per financial year; a 20% TCS applies above this threshold.

faq.q: Is TCS an extra tax I have to pay?
faq.a: No, TCS is not an extra tax. It is an advance tax collected by the authorised dealer. This amount is adjusted against your income tax liability when you file your Income Tax Return or can be claimed as a refund if there's an excess.

faq.q: Should I always pay in local currency when using my card abroad?
faq.a: Yes, always choose to pay in the local currency of the country you are visiting. Opting to pay in Indian Rupees (INR) via Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC) often results in less favourable exchange rates and additional markups from the merchant or their payment processor.

faq.q: Are zero-markup credit cards truly free of all foreign transaction costs?
faq.a: Zero-markup credit cards typically waive the bank's foreign transaction fee, converting at interbank rates. However, you might still encounter local ATM fees for cash withdrawals or charges for specific cross-currency transactions depending on the card's terms.

faq.q: How much cash should I carry for an international trip?
faq.a: It's advisable to carry a small amount of local currency cash for immediate expenses upon arrival (e.g., airport transfer, first meal) and for daily small purchases, tips, and places where cards aren't accepted. Avoid carrying large sums due to security risks.

fact_check.summary: The article provides a generally reliable overview of international travel finances, including forex cards, zero-markup credit cards, cash, and TCS rules. However, some specific details regarding the effective date of IDFC FIRST Bank's zero-markup policy and the current TCS applicability on international credit card spending need correction or clarification.

corrections.note: Corrected information regarding TCS applicability on international credit card spending, clarifying that it is currently deferred from LRS inclusion.

edits.why: International credit card spending abroad is currently deferred from LRS inclusion and does not attract TCS as of mid-2026. This deferral has been in place since 2023.
